subject.title: [Feature]: GitHub Copilot provider cannot reach GitHub Enterprise data-residency (*.ghe.com) tenants

question: Should the bundled github-copilot provider accept allowlisted *.ghe.com tenant routing for auth, token exchange, runtime, embeddings, and usage, or should GHE Copilot remain external/plugin scope?
rationale: VISION.md supports setup reliability and major model provider support, but also routes optional integrations toward plugins; this request is narrower than a new provider because github-copilot is already bundled, yet it still changes config/env surface and token host security behavior.

options.title: Accept narrow bundled-provider routing
options.body: Review and harden the linked PR so the existing github-copilot provider supports github.com and allowlisted single-label *.ghe.com tenant roots without changing public GitHub behavior.

options.title: Route GHE Copilot to plugin scope
options.body: Reject bundled-provider host routing and close this issue plus the linked PR with a clear direction that tenant-specific Copilot support belongs in an installable provider/plugin.

options.title: Require a generic host-routing contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause the linked PR until maintainers define a reusable provider-auth host-routing contract for bundled providers.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow bundled-provider routing
recommendation.body: Review and harden the linked PR so the existing github-copilot provider supports github.com and allowlisted single-label *.ghe.com tenant roots without changing public GitHub behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent current-main signal across the relevant Copilot provider/auth paths and adjacent provider hardening work.
